rows.description: I trusted a junior with a big task and they failed, and now I doubt my ability to delegate. I review what I explained, adjust the scope and check-ins, and delegate again in smaller steps instead of taking everything back.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, favouritism, protectiveness, resentment, shame

rows.description: I find myself helping the junior who reminds me of me and neglecting the awkward one. I catch this bias, give each person equal time and clear expectations, and judge work by evidence, not by comfort.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, disillusionment, protectiveness, resentment, shame

rows.description: My manager thinks I am underperforming but never explained what good looks like and I feel resentful. I ask for concrete examples and goals, and raise unclear expectations respectfully rather than complaining behind their back.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, disillusionment, favouritism, protectiveness, shame

rows.description: I cover for my junior's mistakes to shield them from blame. A little cover early can help, but if I hide problems they never learn; I coach them to own their errors and I stay honest with my boss.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, disillusionment, favouritism, resentment, shame

rows.description: Your boss blames you for a junior's failures. Take responsibility for what you own, explain the coaching you gave, and ask for support in resourcing. Do not scapegoat the junior to save yourself.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, disillusionment, favouritism, protectiveness, resentment

rows.description: My manager gave the credit or the promotion to someone else and I burn with anger. I let the first surge pass, collect facts, ask for a private explanation, and decide whether to stay; a public outburst rarely helps.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, favouritism, fear, gratitude, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: I know a decision is unfair but I am afraid to speak because I need the job. I weigh risk honestly, find allies, raise concerns in writing calmly, and accept that silence is a choice with its own costs.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, favouritism, gratitude, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: My manager clearly favours a colleague and I feel overlooked and small. I check what I can control, make my results visible, ask for clear criteria, and consider moving on if the pattern is fixed.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, fear, gratitude, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: My manager praises me and piles on extra work, hinting that loyalty means unpaid hours. I feel flattered and trapped. I set limits, clarify scope in writing, and notice when praise is used as pay.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, favouritism, fear, gratitude, loyalty

rows.description: My manager backed me when others doubted me and I feel deep gratitude. I honour it with excellence and honesty, and I keep my own judgment; gratitude is not a reason to overlook their mistakes.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, contempt, favouritism, fear, loyalty, manipulation
